title: Psychological resources of readiness for professional self-determination: Meta-analysis
abstract: Context and relevance. A noticeable trend in the latest studies of sustainable professional development of the individual is the search and analysis of its psychological resources. Despite the large amount of accumulated empirical data, the problem of their fragmentation actualizes the prospects for complex studies that could deeply and comprehensively reveal the specifics of relationship between various aspects of professional development and the resources that provide it. Objective. The study had its purpose to use meta-analysis methods to consider how various psychological resources influence students’ readiness for professional self-determination. Methods and materials. Searching for publications for the period from 2019 to 2024 was conducted in 4 databases (ResearchGate, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, Elibrary); 49 works were selected (8 in Russian and 41 in English) with a total of 25,843 subjects. The random-effects model was used for evaluating the effect sizes of psychological resources of readiness for professional self-determination at the level of individual studies. Meta-regression analysis was implemented for a generalized assessment of the contributions of various psychological resources to the students’ readiness for professional self-determination. Results. The meta-analysis demonstrated a significant influence of regulatory, motivational and emotional resources on the students’ readiness for professional self-determination. The effects and contribution of self-positioning, according to the effect size analysis and meta-regression, were insignificant or, in the case of certain aspects of professional self-determination, had moderate significant values. Conclusions. The study confirmed the effects and general contribution of psychological resources to the students’ readiness for professional self-determination. The most significant predictors of readiness for professional self-determination are, first of all, regulatory, personality, emotional and motivational resources. Prospects for further research may be associated with implementing narrow meta-analyses focused on studying the specific effects of certain psychological resources in relation to particular aspects of professional self-determination of an individual.
